_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mali covering Djenné-Djenno, Ghana Empire, Mali Empire (Sundiata/Mansa Musa), Songhai Empire, Timbuktu scholarship, French Sudan, Keita/Traoré eras, 2012 crisis, and jihadist insurgency.

ethnic_groups.name: Bambara (Bamana)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; Mande; central/southern Mali; Bambara language lingua franca; Bamako; Segu kingdom heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Fula/Fulani (Peul)
ethnic_groups.notes: Pastoralists and settled; Macina region; Islamic scholarship; Fula Empire of Macina 1818–1862

ethnic_groups.name: Sarakole/Soninke
ethnic_groups.notes: Mande; descendants of Ghana Empire; Kayes region; migration tradition (Soninké in France)

ethnic_groups.name: Senufo (Senoufo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Mali; Sikasso region; cross-border with Burkina Faso and Ivory Coast; Poro secret society

ethnic_groups.name: Dogon
ethnic_groups.notes: Bandiagara Escarpment; unique cosmology and architecture; resist Islamization; granaries; Sirius B astronomical knowledge claim

ethnic_groups.name: Songhai
ethnic_groups.notes: Gao and Niger River valley; Songhai Empire heritage; merchants and farmers

ethnic_groups.name: Tuareg (Kel Tamasheq)
ethnic_groups.notes: Saharan Berbers; northern Mali; Timbuktu, Gao, Kidal; nomadic heritage; Azawad separatism; MNLA rebels 2012; Tifinagh script

ethnic_groups.name: Malinke/Mandinka (Maninka)
ethnic_groups.notes: Mande; western Mali; Mali Empire heartland; Sundiata Keita heritage; griots/jeli oral tradition

ethnic_groups.name: Bobo
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Mali; Mande-related; Bobo-Dioulasso region; Bwa/Bobo masks

ethnic_groups.name: Moor/Maure
ethnic_groups.notes: Arab-Berber; northern Mali; nomadic; Hassaniya Arabic

independence.notes: Part of Mali Federation with Senegal (June–August 1960) before full independence

current_leader.name: Assimi Goïta
current_leader.title: Transitional President
current_leader.notes: Colonel; led 2020 and 2021 coups; expelled French forces; turned to Russia/Wagner Group; promised elections

former_leaders.name: Modibo Keïta
former_leaders.notes: First president; US-RDA party; socialist; Mali Federation; overthrown by Traoré

former_leaders.name: Moussa Traoré
former_leaders.notes: Military dictator; 23 years; economic decline; 1991 protests; overthrown by Touré

former_leaders.name: Alpha Oumar Konaré
former_leaders.notes: First democratically elected; ADEMA; Timbuktu manuscripts preservation

former_leaders.name: Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT)
former_leaders.notes: Former general; 'soldier of democracy' (led 1991 transition); 2012 coup amid Tuareg rebellion

former_leaders.name: Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta (IBK)
former_leaders.notes: RPM; post-2012 crisis; jihadist insurgency; ousted in 2020 coup; died 2022

910.name: Ancient Civilisations of the Niger Bend
910.description: Early ironworking, agricultural settlement, and rise of Djenné-Djenno as one of Africa's oldest cities.

sub_clusters.name: Saharan Neolithic and Early Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Pastoral and agricultural communities in the desiccating Sahara migrate southward to the Niger River basin.

sub_clusters.name: Djenné-Djenno Urban Centre
sub_clusters.description: One of sub-Saharan Africa's earliest urban centres; iron smelting, rice cultivation, and long-distance trade without centralised state.

910.name: Ghana Empire (Wagadu)
910.description: Soninke-led Ghana Empire dominates trans-Saharan gold-salt trade from its capital Koumbi Saleh.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of the Ghana Empire
sub_clusters.description: Soninke clans unify under the Ghana (war chief); control of gold fields of Bambuk and Bure.

sub_clusters.name: Trans-Saharan Gold-Salt Trade
sub_clusters.description: Ghana taxes gold-salt exchange; Arab geographers describe fabulous wealth; Koumbi Saleh flourishes.

sub_clusters.name: Almoravid Pressure and Decline
sub_clusters.description: Almoravid conquest or pressure on Ghana c.1076; empire fragments into successor states.

920.name: Mali Empire
920.description: Sundiata Keita founds the Mali Empire; Mansa Musa's legendary hajj; Timbuktu becomes centre of Islamic learning.

sub_clusters.name: Sundiata Keita and the Battle of Kirina
sub_clusters.description: Sundiata defeats Sumanguru at Kirina 1235; Kouroukan Fouga charter; Mande heartland unified.

sub_clusters.name: Mansa Musa and the Golden Hajj
sub_clusters.description: Mansa Musa's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca distributes so much gold it depresses Cairo markets; Mali appears on European maps.

sub_clusters.name: Timbuktu as Centre of Learning
sub_clusters.description: Sankore Mosque and university; manuscript tradition; Islamic jurisprudence; scholars like Ahmed Baba.

sub_clusters.name: Decline of the Mali Empire
sub_clusters.description: Succession crises; Songhai and Mossi raids; loss of peripheral provinces; Mali reduced to Mande core.

930.name: Songhai Empire
930.description: Songhai Empire under Sunni Ali and Askia Muhammad becomes the largest empire in African history; Moroccan invasion ends it.

sub_clusters.name: Sunni Ali Ber's Conquests
sub_clusters.description: Sunni Ali captures Timbuktu (1468) and Djenné (1473); builds Songhai into a major empire.

sub_clusters.name: Askia Muhammad's Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: Askia Muhammad usurps power; pilgrimage to Mecca; administrative reforms; Islamic scholarship peaks.

sub_clusters.name: Moroccan Invasion and Fall of Songhai
sub_clusters.description: Saadian Morocco's musketeers defeat Songhai at Battle of Tondibi 1591; empire collapses; region fragments.

930.name: Post-Songhai Successor States
930.description: Bambara kingdoms (Ségou, Kaarta), Fulani jihad states, and Toucouleur Empire fill the power vacuum.

sub_clusters.name: Bambara Kingdoms of Ségou and Kaarta
sub_clusters.description: Biton Coulibaly founds Ségou kingdom; Bambara resist Islam; slave-raiding warrior states.

sub_clusters.name: Fulani Jihad State of Masina
sub_clusters.description: Seku Amadu's jihad establishes theocratic Masina Empire based at Hamdallahi; strict Islamic governance.

940.name: French Sudan (Colonial Mali)
940.description: French military conquest; resistance of Samori Ture and El Hadj Umar; French Sudan within AOF.

sub_clusters.name: El Hadj Umar Tall's Toucouleur Empire
sub_clusters.description: Umar Tall's jihad conquers Bambara states; Toucouleur Empire resists French expansion until defeated.

sub_clusters.name: French Military Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Gallieni and Archinard campaigns; fall of Ségou 1890; Samori Ture captured 1898; colony established.

sub_clusters.name: French Sudan within AOF
sub_clusters.description: Forced labour, head tax, cotton cultivation; Office du Niger irrigation scheme; slow urbanisation.

950.name: Independence and Modibo Keita Era
950.description: Mali Federation with Senegal; independence 1960; Keita's socialist one-party state; 1968 military coup.

sub_clusters.name: Mali Federation with Senegal
sub_clusters.description: Short-lived Mali Federation; Senegal secedes August 1960; Republic of Mali declared.

sub_clusters.name: Modibo Keita's Socialist State
sub_clusters.description: Single-party US-RDA rule; nationalisation; withdrawal from CFA franc; economic difficulties.

950.name: Moussa Traoré Military Rule
950.description: Lieutenant Traoré overthrows Keita; single-party UDPM rule; Sahel droughts; democratic movement topples him.

sub_clusters.name: Traoré Coup and UDPM Rule
sub_clusters.description: Military junta becomes single-party state; Sahel famines 1970s–1980s; Tuareg grievances mount.

sub_clusters.name: 1991 Democratic Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Pro-democracy protests; Amadou Toumani Touré leads military ouster of Traoré; transition to democracy.

960.name: Democratic Mali and the 2012 Crisis
960.description: Multiparty democracy; Tuareg rebellions; 2012 crisis (MNLA, Ansar Dine, French intervention); ongoing jihadist insurgency; military coups.

sub_clusters.name: Third Republic Democracy
sub_clusters.description: Alpha Oumar Konaré and ATT presidencies; Mali hailed as African democratic model; decentralisation.

sub_clusters.name: 2012 Northern Mali Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Tuareg MNLA rebellion; Ansar Dine and AQIM seize northern Mali; coup in Bamako; French Operation Serval.

sub_clusters.name: Ongoing Jihadist Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: JNIM and ISGS attacks spread to central Mali; UN MINUSMA peacekeepers; intercommunal violence.

sub_clusters.name: 2020–2021 Military Coups and Wagner Era
sub_clusters.description: Coups in 2020 and 2021; Colonel Assimi Goïta leads junta; France expelled; Russian Wagner Group deployed; MINUSMA withdrawn.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
